# Palamedes

[![Powered by Sebastian Software](https://img.shields.io/badge/Powered_by-Sebastian_Software-005164?style=flat)](https://oss.sebastian-software.com) [![CI](https://github.com/sebastian-software/palamedes/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/sebastian-software/palamedes/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![License: MIT OR Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-0f172a.svg)](https://github.com/sebastian-software/palamedes#license)

Open-source i18n tooling for TypeScript applications: write messages next to
your code, keep translations in your repository, and use a Rust-powered
toolchain from extraction to runtime.

**[Website](https://palamedes.dev)** ·
**[Documentation](https://palamedes.dev/docs)** ·
**[Frameworks and live demos](https://palamedes.dev/frameworks)** ·
**[Benchmarks](https://palamedes.dev/proof)**

**Palamedes 2.0 is out.** The
[v2 release notes](https://palamedes.dev/docs/release-notes-v2) explain what
changed, and the [migration guide](https://palamedes.dev/docs/migration-v2)
walks you through the upgrade from 1.x.

## What Palamedes Does

- **Author messages in code.** TypeScript and JSX macros cover interpolation,
  plurals, selects, and rich text, with `message + context` as message identity.
- **Keep catalogs in Git.** Source-string-first PO catalogs, optional FCL
  storage, semantic merging, and a Git merge driver support local workflows.
- **Automate translation checks.** The `pmds` CLI extracts and watches sources,
  checks catalog drift, lints authoring, audits ICU compatibility, reports
  translation coverage, and hosts configured binary plugins. Agents can check
  changed source files directly with `pmds lint <files> --json --fail-on warning`.
- **Delegate catalog delivery.** V2 adapters load compiled translations for
  the active locale, including lazy browser dependencies, without app-owned
  catalog maps. Server runtimes isolate request state and share immutable
  compiled catalogs.

The local workflow needs no account or managed service. See the
[architecture](https://palamedes.dev/architecture) for the source-to-runtime
model and [proof](https://palamedes.dev/proof) for reproducible measurements.

## Integrations

| Application | Integration |
| --- | --- |
| React and Solid | Translation components, macros, and headless locale helpers; Vite integration, including MDX. |
| Next.js, TanStack Start, Solid Start, and React Router | Framework integration for server rendering and browser delivery. TanStack Start is verified with React; Solid uses Solid 2 Start Mode with Nitro. |
| Remix v3 and Waku | Dedicated adapters, verified with Remix 3.0.0 and Waku 1.0.0-rc.4. |
| Vue 3 and Svelte 5 | Preview component-script macros and catalog delivery through Vite. Template-text extraction and rich-text components are outside the current scope. |
| Nuxt and SvelteKit | Separate Preview proofs for Node SSR, hydration, lazy loading, and request isolation. No dedicated npm packages are published. |
| Node.js backends | Request-local i18n for Hono, Express, and custom servers. |
| Rust applications | Preview build integration and an external-catalog runtime, published on crates.io as `palamedes-build` and `palamedes-i18n`. |

Use the [framework overview](https://palamedes.dev/frameworks) to choose a host
and try its demos. The [stability policy](https://palamedes.dev/docs/stability)
defines the supported boundaries, including the Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, and SvelteKit
proofs. The [backend guide](https://palamedes.dev/docs/backend-servers) and
[Rust guide](https://palamedes.dev/docs/rust-applications) cover non-browser apps.

Native platform packages are selected by `@palamedes/cli` and
`@palamedes/core-node`. Node.js requirements vary by package; see the
[platform support table](docs/platform-support.md#nodejs-requirements).
The repository Node badge above describes the development and CI requirement.

`palamedes` and `create-palamedes` are reserved names with placeholder commands.
They do not provide an application installer or project generator.
